ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $D$ is a point on side $BC$, with $AB=AD=DC$. If $ \angle B=60^\circ$, find the measure of $ \angle C$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB=AD, \angle B=60^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\triangle ABD$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
therefore $\angle ADB=60^\circ$,\\
since $AD=DC$,\\
it implies that $\angle C=\angle DAC=\frac{1}{2}\angle ADB=\boxed{30^\circ}$

method.method_draft: Use an analytic-coordinate setup based on the diagram. Read from the figure that B, D, C are collinear horizontally with D between B and C, and A is above the base with AB making the given 60° angle at B. From the text set the common length AB=AD=DC to 1. Place B=(0,0) and the base BC on the positive x-axis. Since ∠B=60° and AB=1, A=(cos60°, sin60°)=(1/2, √3/2). Let D=(t,0) on the base. The condition AD=1 gives (t−1/2)^2+(√3/2)^2=1, so t=0 or t=1; reject t=0 because D is not B, hence D=(1,0). Since DC=1 and C is to the right of D, C=(2,0).
